text:
Maria: FYI CS reported a high-severity latency escalation from acct acme-io. They see sporadic p99s ~700ms-1.2s hitting their production app starting around 2025-01-14 02:50 UTC. They included a few request IDs and traces.

Jon: Got it. Can you drop the root thread_ts? I'll start by checking Prometheus histograms and our Grafana panels. If p95 is normal but p99 jumps, common causes: small # of slow samples, promql/windowing artifacts, or coarse histogram buckets.

Maria: thread_ts = 1755654321. CS attached trace ids: t-2025-11, t-2037-02, t-2098-07 (their internal ids map to our traces). They appear in the same spike windows.

Ashley: Note — we rolled runtime batching changes yesterday to tweak low-qps batch thresholds. Canary went out at ~2025-01-14T02:43Z on a subset of nodes.

deploy-bot: Deployment "runtime-batch-tune" started (canary) by Ashley at 2025-01-14T02:43:21Z.

Kevin: I'll pull the raw bucket counts. Quick checklist: (1) confirm dashboard promql uses histogram_quantile vs summaries, (2) compare server-side vs client-side p99 definitions (client includes network & retry), (3) look for exemplars linking buckets to traces.

Jon: Current dashboard query for p99 gen latency is:

```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(gen_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

But our default le boundaries are sparse: [0.01,0.03,0.06,0.12,0.25,0.5,1,2,5] which makes interpolation above 0.5s coarse and sensitive to a few samples.

Maria: CS says 700-1200ms which sits in that wide bucket (0.5,1] or (1,2] depending on value. So histogram_quantile can produce stepy p99s there.

Ashley: Canary timing aligns with first visible bump. The batch sizing increase would raise queuing for long sequences under certain patterns.

Kevin: I computed a bucket-diff over the spike window:

```
(sum(rate(gen_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="1"}[5m]))) - (sum(rate(gen_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="0.5"}[5m])))
```

Thereis a clear blip coincident with the canary start, small absolute count but large relative change because of low baseline.

Maria: Are we sure CS's p99 is the same thing? Their telemetry includes client-side metrics and may capture retries/backoff delays.

Jon: I inspected a couple traces that CS attached. Server-side token-generation time is often ~200-400ms; end-to-end includes queuing and one retry for a subset, pushing the client view into the 700-1200ms range.

Ashley: I rolled the canary back at 2025-01-14T04:10Z because of the correlation.

deploy-bot: Rollback "runtime-batch-tune" executed by Ashley at 2025-01-14T04:11:05Z.

Kevin: After rollback, our Grafana p99 dropped closer to historic levels but CS still reports occasional tails. Sounds like multiple contributors: (A) the canary introduced measurable tails, (B) existing coarse buckets amplify apparent jumps, (C) intermittent infra pressure (GC/preemptions) occasionally add latency.

Jon: Also discovered dashboard mismatch: product-dashboard uses rate() across many replicas before summing, while sla-dashboard uses increase() then divides. For sparse/low-volume windows that difference can skew percentiles because of aggregation ordering.

Maria: So root causes hypothesized: runtime batching change (canary) increased some request durations; promql/dashboard aggregation differences; and coarse histogram buckets produce noisy p99 interpolation. Mitigations needed short-term and medium-term.

Ashley: Short-term actions: (1) confirm canary fully rolled back (done), (2) add a temporary alert on bucket delta for (0.5,1] > 2x baseline, (3) provide a customer-facing explanation and ETA.

Kevin: Medium-term: emit finer histogram buckets around 0.3-1.5s (e.g., add 0.6,0.75,0.9,1.2) and/or publish a summary metric with explicit quantiles for high-cardinality routes. We should also turn on exemplars for gen_request_duration_seconds_bucket so slow bucket increments can reference traces.

Jon: I'll patch dashboards to show both histogram_quantile(0.99, ...) and the raw bucket diffs side-by-side to make interpolation artifacts visible to SRE and PMs. Example queries for the diff panel:

```
sum by (le) (rate(gen_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))

(sum(rate(gen_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="1"}[5m])) - sum(rate(gen_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="0.5"}[5m])))
```

This should help visually confirm a small number of requests crossing the 0.5s->1s boundary.

Maria: Can we reproduce? CS gave a sample payload and QPS patterns. Ashley, can you spin staging with the canary batch config (gitrev abc123) and run their payload at ~20 qps with the same sequence lengths?

Ashley: Yes. I'll spin a staging cluster with the exact batch hints and run the replay. If we reproduce, we'll capture traces and exemplars.

Kevin: I've opened PR 402 in prometheus-instrumentation to add extra buckets. CI passed in staging: PR 402. Note that changing buckets is non-reversible for historical data; we must annotate dashboards and warn customers that past p99s are not recomputable.

deploy-bot: PR 402 merged by Kevin at 2025-01-14T08:22:09Z. CI: green. Scheduled rollout pending maintenance window.

Jon: Important note to SRE/engineering: histogram_quantile is an estimate and sensitive to bucket boundaries. When traffic is low, a handful of requests moving into the next bucket can create a large step in the estimated percentile. This often creates disputes with client-side p99 which uses raw sample quantiles.

Maria: Drafting the CS response. Proposed text:

"Thanks for the report — we traced the issue to a canary change to runtime batching that increased queuing for some long sequences, resulting in a small number of higher-latency requests. We rolled the canary back and see reduced tails. Additionally, our telemetry uses histogram_quantile over coarse buckets which can exaggerate p99 steps; we're adding finer buckets and exemplars to map slow buckets back to traces. Short-term: alerting added and monitoring intensified. Medium-term: metrics bucket update and exemplar rollout in 2-5 days. We'll follow up with a postmortem and timeline." :thumbsup:

Kevin: Suggest including ETAs: metrics buckets and dashboards (2 days), exemplar rollout & trace linking (3-5 days). I'll schedule prod rollout in the next maintenance window and ping oncall.

Maria: Action items recap:
- Ashley: send CS reply now and attach estimated timelines (in 30m)
- Kevin: coordinate prod rollout of bucket changes (post-maint window) and enable exemplars in staging
- Jon: update Grafana panels to show both quantile & bucket diffs, annotate dashboard change window
- Maria: keep CS engaged and attach escalation timeline; own postmortem

escalation-bot: Escalation updated for acme-io severity=high, owners=[Maria,Ashley,Kevin] at 2025-01-14T09:01:00Z.

Maria: Leaving thread open until postmortem complete. Thanks everyone for quick response.
